_note: Channel manifest for recursive.eco. This is the file the app actually reads — `POST /api/channel/import-from-github` fetches `recursive-eco.json` from the repo root (raw first, GitHub-App contents-API fallback, so it works while the repo is PRIVATE) and requires `channel.slug` + `channel.name`. It then reads `grammars.id_map` for the slug→UUID map and takes the folder prefix from `grammars.paths[0]` to hash each `<prefix><slug>/grammar.json` as the drift baseline. There is no `channel.json` in this design; that name is read by nothing. See recursive-eco/docs/future_plan/DESIGN-github-sync-and-contribution.md.

channel.name: Recursive Learning
channel.description: Recursive eco-improvement: the film, the game, and the grammars about AI and how we learn with it — one channel, bound to its GitHub repo.

hero.title: Recursive Learning
hero.subtitle: We're here to do recursive eco-improvement — and to test that hypothesis at the sizes we actually work at.
hero.body_md:
Recursive self-improvement can fail in several ways, because a thing that improves itself still has to adapt with its environment, or adapt the environment. This channel is where that hypothesis gets tested small: films assembled out of other people's footage, courses that teach the tools, and grammars that hold the questions rather than the answers.

Everything here is a grammar — a sequence you can open, star, fork, and correct. Open one, star it, and it lands on your own channel.

grammars._exclude_note: Nothing generated or apparatus-only lives here yet. Private grammars are simply absent — they are indexed by name + id in grammars/PRIVATE.md and appear here only if she publishes them and the export script is re-run.

_source_of_truth_note: `source_of_truth` is a property of the CHANNEL DOCUMENT in recursive.eco (`document_data.source_of_truth = 'repo'`), not of this file — the importer does not copy it from the manifest today. Declared here as intent; see docs/CHANNELS.md for the three steps that make it true.
